item.title: Cardinals bid farewell to Nationals, Busch Stadium for 2026
item.description: The visiting Washington Nationals will look to complete a three-game sweep of the St. Louis Cardinals on Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The visiting Washington Nationals will look to complete a three-game sweep of the St. Louis Cardinals on Sunday afternoon. It will be the final home game of the season for the Cardinals, who are 37-43 at Busch Stadium. On Saturday, the Nationals scored four runs in the top of the 11th inning and held on for an 8-5 win. Washington (73-82) has won six of its past seven games, and a victory Sunday would give the team a .500 mark in September (8-8) despite a recent seven-game losing streak. The Cardinals (75-80), meanwhile, have lost four games in a row. After Sunday's game, they will finish the season at Pittsburgh and Milwaukee. Both St. Louis and Washington sit fourth in their respective divisions with seven games remaining, and both have been eliminated from postseason contention. The Nationals will start right-hander Jake Irvin (2-9, 5.51 ERA) on Sunday, and the Cardinals will counter with rookie left-hander Quinn Mathews (2-3, 3.62). Irvin has struggled since returning from the injured list in late July, going 0-5 with a 5.84 ERA in nine games (eight starts). Last time out, he followed an opener for the first time in his four-year career and gave up three runs on two hits and four walks over five innings against the Los Angeles Angels on Sept. 12. He struck out six and didn't figure into the decision of a 6-5 loss in 10 innings. Irvin has allowed 16 first-inning runs in 19 starts this season. Mathews will make his eighth major league start. Over his past four starts, he is 2-1 with a 1.93 ERA. In his most recent game, he allowed one run on four hits over 6 2/3 innings of a 2-1 win Monday against the San Francisco Giants. He struck out a career-high eight batters and walked two. He retired the first 10 batters he faced and did not allow a hit until the sixth. "(Catcher Leo Bernal) kind of navigated the first three innings -- I think I shook one pitch in three innings, which is unbelievable, to be honest with you," Mathews said. "So a lot of credit to Bernal there, getting me through the first three when I wasn't as sharp as I would have liked to have been." Saturday night, the Nationals won despite blowing their 40th and 41st save chances of the season, losing a 3-2 lead in the ninth and a 4-3 lead in the 10th. Jose Tena had the big hit in the 11th, a two-run double, and the bullpen held on, with Will Dion getting the final out for his first major league save. Washington's Jorbit Vivas had four hits, and Daylen Lile smacked a two-run homer. Jose Fermin and Ivan Herrera had three hits each for St. Louis. The Cardinals pulled to 8-5 and loaded the bases with no outs in the bottom of the 11th, but Nationals relievers retired three hitters in a row -- two by strikeout -- to end the game. For the game, St. Louis was called for a catcher's interference, committed two errors and left 13 men on base. "They've done a really nice job of playing some pretty clean baseball," manager Oliver Marmol said of his team, "and even when we don't, you have the winning run up to the plate in extra innings. There's parts of that game that are highly frustrating." --Field Level Media

item.title: Rangers look for length from Jacob deGrom in finale vs. Jays
item.description: The Texas Rangers have had to turn to their bullpen more often than they would have liked in the first two contests of their three-game series against the Toronto Blue Jays in Arlington, Texas.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Texas Rangers have had to turn to their bullpen more often than they would have liked in the first two contests of their three-game series against the Toronto Blue Jays in Arlington, Texas. After pulling starter Kumar Rocker in the fifth inning of Friday's 7-1 win, Texas manager Skip Schumaker was forced to go to his bullpen with one out in the second on Saturday after starter Cal Quantrill exited the game with right lat tightness. Jordan Montgomery stepped in and held Toronto hitless over 3 2/3 innings in a 6-2 victory. Schumaker hopes to give his relievers a breather when Jacob deGrom takes the mound in the finale against the Blue Jays on Sunday afternoon. "That's what this team is all about right now," Schumaker said. "... Monty was fantastic. But again, these are team wins, and it's also because of what happened the day before, really covering us today." The veteran deGrom (11-9, 3.79 ERA) has been strong at home this season. The right-hander has a 2.53 ERA with 111 strikeouts in 85 1/3 innings over 15 starts at Globe Life Field. He's coming off an outing in which he allowed just two runs on three hits in five innings against the Boston Red Sox on Sept. 15. He has only made three starts against the Blue Jays in his career, going 1-1 with a 1.65 ERA. The Rangers (78-77) are eyeing a third straight win and a seventh in eight games. Saturday's victory combined with the Houston Astros' loss to the Atlanta Braves, propelled Texas into sole possession of first place in the American League West. "We're just here showing up every day to play and try and get in the playoffs," outfielder Wyatt Langford said. "To be in that position right now is great. But yeah, there are still a lot of games left. We need to keep it that way." While the playoff picture is looking up for Texas, the hopes continue to fade for Toronto (76-79), which has dropped four of its past five. The loss dropped the Blue Jays to three games behind the final wild card in the AL, currently held by the Chicago White Sox, with seven games remaining in the season. Toronto trailed 3-0 after two innings. The Blue Jays didn't get their first baserunner until Vladimir Guerrero Jr. walked in the fourth inning, and didn't get their first hit until the sixth. But pitching struggles in the bottom of the sixth allowed the Rangers to tack on three more runs. "It feels like the last couple games you're down early, and it makes it a little bit tougher to come back," manager John Schneider said. "You're looking for a big swing, a three-run homer or a base hit to score a couple to get back into it. I think falling behind early makes it a little bit tougher." Spencer Miles (6-2, 2.65) will get the start in what is expected to be a bullpen game for Toronto on Sunday. It'll be the second career appearance against Texas for the 26-year-old righty, who gave up just one hit in 2 2/3 innings of a relief appearance in a no-decision versus the Rangers on June 26. --Field Level Media

item.title: Irán advierte de una nueva escalada de Estados Unidos y sus aliados
item.description: Irán advirtió el domingo contra cualquier nuevo ataque de gran envergadura de Estados Unidos y sus aliados, y dijo que disponía de información según la cual se estaba preparando una acción de este tipo, lo que aumentó la inquietud en una región ya sacudida por los ataques con drones y misiles contra Arabia Saudita .
item.dc:creator: Jana Choukeir
item.content:encoded: Irán advirtió el domingo contra cualquier nuevo ataque de gran envergadura de Estados Unidos y sus aliados, y dijo que disponía de información según la cual se estaba preparando una acción de este tipo, lo que aumentó la inquietud en una región ya sacudida por los ataques con drones y misiles contra Arabia Saudita . El mando central militar de Irán dijo en medios de comunicación estatales que cualquier nuevo ataque desencadenaría una represalia sostenida contra las bases y los intereses estadounidenses, y que los aliados regionales de Washington serían considerados partes en el conflicto. No dio más detalles sobre la información de la que, dijo, disponía acerca de un inminente ataque estadounidense. El Departamento de Estado de Estados Unidos emitió el sábado una alerta de seguridad en la que indicaba que existía la posibilidad de una escalada imprevista en Oriente Medio y que los estadounidenses debían redoblar la vigilancia y estar atentos a posibles cancelaciones de vuelos y cierres del espacio aéreo. A punto de cumplirse siete meses de la guerra entre Estados Unidos e Irán, ninguna de las partes parece dispuesta a hacer concesiones importantes para poner fin a los combates y, con los mercados energéticos mundiales ya al límite, el conflicto sigue extendiéndose en la región. El sábado, los hutíes de Yemen, respaldados por Irán, dijeron haber llevado a cabo ataques en la capital saudita, Riad, y contra una importante instalación petrolera en el puerto de Yanbu, en el mar Rojo. Arabia Saudita no hizo comentarios sobre el incidente ni sobre las afirmaciones de los hutíes. La alerta del Departamento de Estado de Estados Unidos mencionaba las hostilidades de los hutíes contra Arabia Saudita, incluidos los aeropuertos civiles. La reciente escalada de los hutíes ha obligado a Riad a enfrentarse a un doloroso dilema: continuar con los ataques aéreos contra el grupo para impedir que se apodere de más territorio yemení o dar un paso atrás con la esperanza de evitar ataques con drones contra infraestructuras críticas. Los avances de los hutíes a lo largo de la costa significan que las fuerzas del grupo se sitúan ahora en el estrecho de Mandeb, lo que les facilita el control del tráfico marítimo entre el mar Rojo y Asia y les permite bloquear esta vía navegable crucial. Dado que Irán ya ha bloqueado la mayor parte del tráfico marítimo en el estrecho de Ormuz, las exportaciones energéticas del golfo Pérsico, rico en petróleo, están ahora casi totalmente aisladas de los mercados mundiales, lo que aumenta la presión sobre los precios mundiales del petróleo. Por su parte, el bloqueo estadounidense de los puertos iraníes impide a Irán vender su propio petróleo, lo que contribuye a los graves problemas de la economía de la República Islámica. Irán reiteró el domingo que no reabriría el estrecho de Ormuz hasta que se cumplan los términos de un acuerdo de junio, tal y como los interpretaba. El presidente del Parlamento iraní, Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf, dijo que Irán tendría que seguir luchando, además de negociando, para hacer retroceder a sus enemigos y consolidar cualquier avance logrado mediante la diplomacia.

item.title: Ronald Acuna Jr., Braves bid to clinch NL East in finale vs. Astros
item.description: Atlanta Braves right fielder Ronald Acuna Jr. rode a torrid 20-game stretch into the middle contest Saturday of an interleague series against the Houston Astros, and he continued his stellar play.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Atlanta Braves right fielder Ronald Acuna Jr. rode a torrid 20-game stretch into the middle contest Saturday of an interleague series against the Houston Astros, and he continued his stellar play. Acuna finished 2-for-3 with two walks and a seventh-inning grand slam that sent the Braves toward a 6-3 victory. Atlanta (91-64) has a magic number of one to clinch the National League East title for the seventh time in nine seasons heading into Sunday's series finale in Houston. Acuna was batting .363 with six homers and 16 RBIs over the previous 20 games, a stretch that started after he sat and watched the finale of a three-game series against the Los Angeles Dodgers on Aug. 27. Since then, he has more closely resembled the two-way threat who terrorized the NL before two separate season-ending knee injuries altered his stardom. "And it's understandable, right?" Braves manager Walt Weiss said of Acuna methodically rounding into his superstar form. "When you have both knees reconstructed, it takes time to, not only physically, but mentally have the confidence in really letting it fly. "I think we're seeing that now with Ronald again." Left-hander Martin Perez (9-9, 3.07 ERA) will start the series finale for the Braves. Perez earned his first win in six starts -- and the 100th victory of his career -- in the Braves' 6-3 triumph over the Chicago Cubs on Tuesday, allowing three runs (two earned) on five hits and four walks with two strikeouts over six innings. Perez was 0-3 with a 3.55 ERA in the five starts between wins, and he is 10-8 with a 3.72 ERA in 22 career appearances (21 starts) against the Astros. Right-hander Hunter Brown (6-3, 3.43 ERA) is scheduled to start for the Astros (77-78) as they attempt to avert a three-game series sweep on Sunday. Houston trails the Texas Rangers by one game atop the American League West and is two games behind the Chicago White Sox in the race for the AL's final wild-card spot. Brown matched his season high with 10 strikeouts against the Kansas City Royals on Tuesday, allowing one run on two hits and three walks over five innings in a 4-2 win. He is 3-0 with a 2.86 ERA over his last five starts. Brown is 1-1 with a 4.15 ERA across three career starts against the Braves. He recorded a 6-2 win over them on Sept. 13, 2025, allowing two runs on four hits and one walk with two strikeouts over 6 2/3 innings. Left-hander Steven Okert, Houston's second-most consistent reliever behind closer Josh Hader, has spent the last two weeks on the injured list with a hamstring strain. His absence continues to be felt, as the Astros have struggled with high-leverage situations. Right-hander reliever AJ Blubaugh allowed three runs on two hits and one walk while recording just one out in the seventh inning on Saturday. In seven appearances since Okert went on the IL, Blubaugh has surrendered nine runs on nine hits and five walks over six innings. Right-hander reliever Bryan Abreu allowed a walk-off home run to the Rays' Junior Caminero on Sept. 11 and surrendered the grand slam to Acuna that flipped the game on Saturday. Previously reliable relievers Blubaugh and Abreu -- in tandem with Okert -- have labored lately. "Those are our guys, and I trust them," Astros manager Joe Espada said. "And I'm going to continue to give them the ball." --Field Level Media

item.title: Iran warns against new escalation by US and allies
item.description: Iran said it had information such a move was being prepared, adding to the anxiety in a region already on edge after drone and missile strikes on Saudi Arabia.
item.dc:creator: Jana Choukeir
item.content:encoded: Iran warned on Sunday against any big new attack by the United States and its allies, saying it had information such a move was being prepared, adding to the anxiety in a region already on edge after drone and missile strikes [USN:L1N45B003 TEXT:"on Saudi Arabia"]. Iran's military central command said on state media that any new attack would trigger sustained retaliation against US bases and interests, and that Washington's regional allies would be considered parties to the conflict. It did not elaborate on the information it said it had about a coming US attack. The US State Department issued a security alert on Saturday saying there was potential for unforeseen escalation in the Middle East and Americans should exercise more vigilance and be aware of possible flight cancellations and airspace closures. Nearly seven months into the US-Iran war , neither side has looked ready to make major concessions needed to end the fighting and with global energy markets already stretched, the conflict continues to spill over into other crises around the region. On Saturday Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis, who made major advances along Yemen's Red Sea coast after the country's civil war reignited this month, said they had carried out strikes in the Saudi capital Riyadh and on a major oil facility in the kingdom's Red Sea port of Yanbu. Reuters video showed a massive plume of black smoke billowing from the area of Riyadh's main international airport after booms were heard in the Saudi capital overnight. Saudi Arabia did not comment on the incident or the Houthi claims, though a Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it had foiled other attacks on the kingdom. The US State Department alert cited Houthi hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including civilian airports. Recent escalation by the Houthis has forced Riyadh into a painful dilemma: continue airstrikes on the group to stop it seizing more Yemeni territory or step back in the hopes of averting drone strikes on critical infrastructure. STRIKES ON SAUDI ARABIA The Houthi gains along the coast mean the group's forces now sit on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, giving them easier control over shipping travelling between the Red Sea and Asia and the ability to blockade the crucial waterway. With Iran already having blockaded most shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, the oil-rich Gulf's energy exports are now almost entirely cut off from global markets, adding to pressure on global oil prices. A US blockade of Iranian ports is meanwhile stopping Iran from selling its own oil, contributing to [USN:L1N44W081 TEXT:"major problems"] in the Islamic Republic's economy. With the war inflicting painful damage on all sides, however, there is little sign of a return to the interim ceasefire agreement that was struck in June but that [USN:L6N43F0R2 TEXT:"fell apart"] in July amid disputes over its terms. Iran reiterated on Sunday that it would not reopen the Strait of Hormuz until the terms of that June agreement, as it interpreted them, were met. Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf said Iran would have to keep on fighting as well as negotiating, to push back its enemies and to consolidate any gains with diplomacy.

item.title: Un Israélien et un Palestinien abattus en Cisjordanie occupée
item.description: Un Israélien a été abattu dimanche en Cisjordanie occupée par un tireur palestinien présumé, a rapporté la police, tandis que des soldats israéliens ont tué un automobiliste palestinien qui, selon l'armée, tentait de les renverser.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Un Israélien a été abattu dimanche en Cisjordanie occupée par un tireur palestinien présumé, a rapporté la police, tandis que des soldats israéliens ont tué un automobiliste palestinien qui, selon l'armée, tentait de les renverser. Selon l'armée et la police israéliennes, le tireur a ouvert le feu depuis son véhicule sur des Israéliens rassemblés à proximité de la colonie de Neve Tzuf, près de Ramallah. Un homme grièvement blessé par balle a été déclaré mort à l'hôpital, a déclaré la police. Le tireur a été localisé quelques heures plus tard dans un hôpital de Ramallah et arrêté, a-t-elle ajouté. Peu après la fusillade, l'armée a annoncé avoir "éliminé" un automobiliste palestinien qui avait tenté de lancer sa voiture sur des soldats près de la colonie de Ganim, plus au nord en Cisjordanie. Aucun soldat n'a été blessé, a-t-elle ajouté.

item.title: El hermano de Diana compara trato que medios dan a Enrique y Meghan con el que sufrió la princesa
item.description: El trato que los medios de comunicación han dispensado al príncipe Enrique y a su esposa Meghan es comparable al que sufrió su madre, Diana, dijo el hermano de la difunta princesa en una entrevista publicada el domingo, en la que advirtió de que era necesario aprender de aquella época.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El trato que los medios de comunicación han dispensado al príncipe Enrique y a su esposa Meghan es comparable al que sufrió su madre, Diana, dijo el hermano de la difunta princesa en una entrevista publicada el domingo, en la que advirtió de que era necesario aprender de aquella época. Diana falleció a los 36 años en un accidente de tráfico en París en 1997, mientras unos fotógrafos la perseguían en moto, lo que desencadenó una oleada de dolor y un debate sobre si los medios de comunicación tenían alguna responsabilidad en su muerte. "Si te fijas en una noticia de un tabloide sobre Diana o sobre la pareja que mencionabas, Enrique y Meghan, ya sabes, pueden ser realmente, realmente desagradables", dijo a la BBC el hermano de Diana, el conde Charles Spencer. "Y creo que la gente debería aprender del ejemplo de Diana". "No estoy aquí para hablar en nombre de Enrique y Meghan, pero para cualquiera que esté siendo destrozado de esta manera a diario, debe de ser una influencia cancerosa en su vida", dijo. Enrique, el hijo menor de Diana, y Meghan, mencionaron el impacto de lo que ellos denominaban "medios tóxicos" tenía en sus vidas antes de renunciar a sus obligaciones reales y mudarse a Estados Unidos en 2020. También demandaron a gran parte de la prensa sensacionalista británica —con diversos grados de éxito— antes de regresar a Gran Bretaña en agosto. Spencer ha acaparado los titulares de todo el mundo durante la última semana después de que su libro, «Swan Song: Diana, My Sister», se publicara por entregas en el Daily Mail, en el que acusaba a su exmarido, el ahora rey Carlos, de mostrarse «eufórico» en las horas posteriores a su muerte. El palacio respondió afirmando que el rey «es consciente de que el dolor de la pérdida de un hermano puede nublar la razón, afectar al juicio y sesgar los recuerdos de formas que los demás no perciben, incluso muchos años después de dicha pérdida». La publicación del libro y el regreso de Harry y Meghan a Gran Bretaña suponen otro reto para el rey, que sigue sometiéndose a tratamiento contra el cáncer. La familia de Diana acusó a la familia real de mostrar una falta de apoyo o de atención hacia la difunta princesa antes de su muerte, una acusación que repitió Harry, quien actualmente se encuentra en gran medida distanciado del resto de la familia real.

item.title: Resurgent Acosta beats Martin for maiden MotoGP win in Austria
item.description: Pedro Acosta claimed the first MotoGP victory of his career in the Austrian Grand Prix on Sunday, bouncing back from his sprint-race crash to beat world championship leader Jorge Martin at KTM's home Red Bull Ring circuit.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Pedro Acosta claimed the first MotoGP victory of his career in the Austrian Grand Prix on Sunday, bouncing back from his [USN:L1N45B02X TEXT:"sprint-race"] crash to beat world championship leader Jorge Martin at KTM's home Red Bull Ring circuit. The 22-year-old Spaniard, who qualified third before crashing out while leading Saturday's sprint, seized the lead from [USN:L4N45B027 TEXT:"polesitter Martin"] on lap nine of the 28-lap race and never looked back. Aprilia's Marco Bezzecchi completed the podium, while Trackhouse rider Ai Ogura finished fourth. It was an emotional moment for Acosta, nicknamed 'The Shark', who arrived in MotoGP with huge expectations after winning the Moto3 world title in 2021 and the Moto2 crown in 2023. "The first one is always special," Acosta said. "Nice way to close a season like this with KTM in front of all Austrian fans. Super happy for them because they deserve it even more than me." Acosta is set to leave KTM at the end of 2026 to join the factory Ducati team. Martin, the 2024 MotoGP champion, got off to a brilliant start but was overtaken by teammate Bezzecchi for the lead at Turn One on lap two. The 28-year-old responded immediately, reclaiming top spot at Turn Three on the same lap. However, Acosta's pace proved decisive and he passed Martin for the lead on lap nine before pulling away. "I want to congratulate Pedro. He fought a lot during the last few years to get this victory. This feeling is amazing for him, so I'm really happy for him," Martin said of his fellow Spaniard. "For myself, I think I did a great race. I was trying to manage the fuel. Then Pedro took me but I thought everything was under control. But step by step, he was stepping away. I tried to push a bit more but my rear tyre was completely destroyed. I did my best. "This is what we have to do every weekend for the rest of the season, and the fight is on. So I am really looking forward to continuing like this." Martin now has 306 points in the standings, a 12-point lead over compatriot and reigning MotoGP champion Marc Marquez ahead of next month's Japanese Grand Prix. Italian Bezzecchi is third with 264 points. Marquez endured a frustrating weekend as Ducati lacked the outright pace of the Aprilias. The seven-time MotoGP champion qualified second but slipped back on the opening lap and eventually finished fifth.

item.title: Cubs eye potential playoff berth in finale vs. Reds
item.description: The Chicago Cubs could not ask for a better gift than a healthy Dansby Swanson for the playoffs.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Chicago Cubs could not ask for a better gift than a healthy Dansby Swanson for the playoffs. Swanson came off the injured list on Friday after being sidelined for a month with a left oblique strain. On Saturday, he hit his 19th home run of the season to help the visiting Cubs record a 5-2 victory over the Cincinnati Reds. Chicago (86-69) can clinch a playoff spot with a win on Sunday afternoon against the Reds and a loss by the Arizona Diamondbacks to the New York Yankees. The Cubs are tied with the San Diego Padres (86-69) in the race for the top wild-card spot in the National League, one game ahead of the Philadelphia Phillies (85-70) and five games ahead of Arizona (81-74). "This is like uncharted territory for me," Swanson said. "I'm just grateful for all the support from the team. Today was just a complete effort from everyone. I love when (reliever Daniel) Palencia is out there and believes no one can hit him. That is when he is best." Palencia retired all six batters he faced in two innings on Saturday, striking out three. "His two innings were his best outing of the year," Cubs manager Craig Counsell said of Palencia. "Through this last week, we have to find out about our bullpen, and this was a good step in that direction." The bullpen took over for Matthew Boyd, who allowed two runs on two hits in five innings to pick up his first win since Aug. 9. Four relievers allowed only two hits the rest of the way. "If we want to be a team that plays for a long time, we need to get outs from the bullpen," Counsell said. "We have to figure out who is going to get it done." The Cubs are expected to send left-hander David Peterson (8-8, 5.11 ERA) to the mound on Sunday. He is coming off a solid start in which he allowed one earned run on three hits in six innings of a 7-3 victory over the Atlanta Braves on Monday. The 31-year-old is 1-2 with a 5.84 ERA in eight career appearances (seven starts) vs. Cincinnati (72-83), which has been eliminated from playoff contention and will counter with right-hander Rhett Lowder (6-11, 5.79 ERA) on Sunday. Lowder's last win came on Aug. 28, a 10-8 decision over the Cubs. He yielded three runs on six hits in five innings to improve to 1-1 with a 3.60 ERA in four career meetings (three starts) vs. Chicago. The 24-year-old is coming off a 4-0 loss to the Dodgers on Tuesday in a game in which he gave up three runs and five hits in five innings. The Reds rallied to forge a 2-2 tie on Saturday with two runs in the fifth inning before the game slipped away. "The only thing I would say is I'm jealous," Cincinnati manager Terry Francona said. "Me and Nap (bench coach Mike Napoli) were talking (Friday) night. We were looking at the scoreboard, like, man, that feeling of anxiety. I kind of miss that." --Field Level Media

item.title: USA Trump transforme son projet d'arc de triomphe en "complexe militaire"
item.description: Le président américain Donald Trump a déclaré dimanche avoir accepté, à la demande de l'armée, de convertir son projet d'arc de triomphe à Washington en complexe militaire chargé d'abriter et déployer drones et munitions.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le président américain Donald Trump a déclaré dimanche avoir accepté, à la demande de l'armée, de convertir son projet d'arc de triomphe à Washington en complexe militaire chargé d'abriter et déployer drones et munitions. Le président américain a mentionné des préoccupations de sécurité nationale à l'appui de cette décision, sans mentionner de menaces spécifiques. Donald Trump a déjà modifié son projet de salle de bal à la Maison blanche, contesté devant la justice, et le présente désormais comme un complexe militaire intégré nécessaire à la sécurité nationale. L'autorité américaine de l'aviation civile a estimé vendredi que le projet d'un arc de triomphe d'une hauteur de 76 mètres près du cimetière national d'Arlington ne présentait pas de risque pour l'aviation civile à condition qu'il soit surmonté en permanence de spots éclairants. Des experts en aéronautique avaient émis des inquiétudes quant au choix du site, non loin de l'aéroport Ronald-Reagan. Des anciens combattants ont également déposé un recours contre le projet en estimant qu'il abîmerait la perspective entre le Lincoln Memorial et le cimetière d'Arlington. Depuis le début de son second mandat en janvier 2025, Donald Trump a entrepris de remodeler en profondeur la capitale fédérale avec la volonté d'y laisser son empreinte. Outre la destruction de l'aile Est de la Maison blanche pour y construire sa salle de bal, le président américain a fait rénover le bassin réfléchissant du Lincoln Memorial, désormais recouvert d'algues, et menace de démolir le Kennedy Center, haut lieu culturel de la ville, depuis que la justice lui a refusé d'y accoler son nom.
